title: overlay-endpoint v1
description: What the separate overlay repository hands Horde, and all it hands it: the output of `horde-overlay endpoint --name <name> --json` (plan step R8, design section 14). Horde owns this schema, because the consumer defines what it needs; the overlay imports nothing of Horde's and Horde imports nothing of its code. An address per peer, this machine's own address and interface, and a health answer. Health is ADVISORY: whether a link exists is decided by the transport's own handshake, so a healthy overlay beside a refused handshake is unknown, link refused. provider is a lower-case word and not a closed list, so a new provider is not a schema change. health is a core/tristate answer as schema/link-frame.v1 writes one - value present exactly when state is known - and remote/Contract.ps1 checks that rule, which this validator cannot state. Output that fails this schema is unknown to Horde, never a guessed address.

address.description: An IPv4 or IPv6 address, as text. A host name is refused: the overlay's job is to resolve one.
